muscular process: Laterally projecting process of the arytenoid; the posterior and lateral cricoarytenoid muscles attach here to open or close the vocal folds.
mylohyoid line: Oblique line on the inner surface of the mandible; mylohyoid, which forms the floor of the mouth, attaches to it.
mylohyoid muscle: Flat muscle forming the floor of the mouth (oral diaphragm); supplied by the nerve to mylohyoid (V3), it raises the floor of the mouth and the tongue during swallowing.
nasal bone: Small, paired, rectangular bone forming the bridge of the nose; the most commonly fractured facial bone.
nasal margin of frontal bone: Margin that articulates with the nasal bones.
nasal part of frontal bone: Part of the frontal bone extending to the root of the nose.
nasal septal cartilage: Quadrilateral hyaline cartilage forming the front of the nasal septum; its deviation causes nasal obstruction.
nasal spine of frontal bone: Small spine supporting the nasal septum.
nasalis muscle: Its transverse part narrows the nostril and its alar part widens it.
navicular articular surface: Surface of the head of the talus that articulates with the navicular.
navicular bone: Boat-shaped tarsal bone between the head of the talus and the cuneiforms; tibialis posterior attaches to its medial tuberosity, and it is the keystone of the medial longitudinal arch.
neck of femur: Neck joining the head to the shaft; it often fractures in the elderly and can lead to avascular necrosis of the head.
neck of fibula: Neck below the head; the common fibular nerve lies against the bone here, and a fracture can cause foot drop.
neck of malleus: Constriction between the head and handle of the malleus.
neck of radius: Constriction between the head and the tuberosity.
neck of rib: Part between the head and the tubercle.
neck of scapula: Constriction just medial to the glenoid.
neck of talus: Constriction between the head and the body; after a fracture here avascular necrosis of the body is common.
neck of tooth: Constriction where the crown meets the root; the gum ends here.
ninth rib: 9th rib: a false (vertebrochondral) rib; its cartilage joins the costal cartilage above.
nuchal ligament: Triangular fibroelastic ligament from the occipital bone to the C7 spine; it helps support the weight of the head and gives attachment to trapezius and splenius.

oblique cord: Small fibrous band running from the ulnar tuberosity to the radius.
oblique head of adductor hallucis: Head arising from the bases of the 2nd–4th metatarsals.
oblique head of adductor pollicis: Arises from the capitate and the bases of the 2nd–3rd metacarpals.
oblique line of mandible: Oblique line on the outer surface; muscles of the corner of the mouth attach to it.
oblique line of thyroid cartilage: Oblique line on the outer surface of the lamina; sternothyroid, thyrohyoid and the inferior constrictor attach to it.
oblique part of cricothyroid muscle: Posterior fibres of cricothyroid, which tenses the vocal folds; it is the only laryngeal muscle supplied by the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve.
oblique popliteal ligament: Extension of the semimembranosus tendon that reinforces the back of the capsule obliquely.
